text_blocks.snippet: Alcohol-related cerebellar ataxia is a condition caused by excessive alcohol consumption, leading to damage in the cerebellum, the part of the brain that controls balance and coordination. This damage results in a range of symptoms including impaired gait, balance problems, and difficulty with fine motor skills.
snippet_highlighted_words: a condition caused by excessive alcohol consumption, leading to damage in the cerebellum, the part of the brain that controls balance and coordination

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of alcohol-related cerebellar ataxia:

list.title: Cause:
list.snippet: Excessive, long-term alcohol use is the primary cause.

list.title: Mechanism:
list.snippet: Alcohol is toxic to the cerebellum, leading to degeneration and shrinkage, particularly in the anterior superior vermis.
